w001.palate: Creamy and intense; fine, persistent bead.
w001.producer: Moët & Chandon's prestige cuvée, named after the 17th-century Benedictine monk of Hautvillers. Made only in declared vintages; the P2 'second plenitude' release rests around 15 years on its lees before disgorging, for more depth and toastiness.
w001.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.

w002.producer: Reims house founded in 1843 by Joseph Krug. Every base wine is fermented in small, old oak casks. The numbered Grande Cuvée editions draw on a huge library of reserve wines; the vintage is made only in exceptional years.
w002.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.

w003.palate: Rich and creamy; fine mousse, long.
w003.producer: Reims house founded in 1843 by Joseph Krug. Every base wine is fermented in small, old oak casks. The numbered Grande Cuvée editions draw on a huge library of reserve wines; the vintage is made only in exceptional years.
w003.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.
w003.vineyard: A blend of many villages and vintages; this edition is based on the 2014 harvest.

w004.producer: Family-owned Épernay house founded in 1849. Winston Churchill was a devoted customer, and the Pinot Noir-led prestige cuvée named after him has been made since the 1975 vintage.
w004.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.

w005.nose: Ripe pear, honey, spice, toasted oak.
w005.producer: Aÿ family house whose family has grown grapes in the village for twelve generations. Pinot Noir-focused and oak-shaped: wines are fermented and aged in barrels made from the nearby Argonne forest.
w005.region: Aÿ, Champagne: a grand cru village on the Marne, historically the most prized source of Champagne Pinot Noir.
w005.vineyard: From Giraud's best Aÿ grand cru parcels.

w006.producer: Aÿ family house whose family has grown grapes in the village for twelve generations. Pinot Noir-focused and oak-shaped: wines are fermented and aged in barrels made from the nearby Argonne forest.
w006.region: Aÿ, Champagne: a grand cru village on the Marne, historically the most prized source of Champagne Pinot Noir.
w006.vineyard: From Giraud's best Aÿ grand cru parcels.

w007.producer: Aÿ family house whose family has grown grapes in the village for twelve generations. Pinot Noir-focused and oak-shaped: wines are fermented and aged in barrels made from the nearby Argonne forest.
w007.region: Aÿ, Champagne: a grand cru village on the Marne, historically the most prized source of Champagne Pinot Noir.
w007.vineyard: Blended from a perpetual reserve of many vintages.

w008.producer: Aÿ family house whose family has grown grapes in the village for twelve generations. Pinot Noir-focused and oak-shaped: wines are fermented and aged in barrels made from the nearby Argonne forest.
w008.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.
w008.vineyard: Named for the chalk (craie) soils of its Chardonnay.

w009.producer: Founded in Reims in 1729, the first established Champagne house. Known for its Chardonnay-led style and its deep chalk cellars (crayères).
w009.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.

w116.nose: Lemon, white flowers, pear, light brioche.
w116.producer: Épernay house founded in 1811 by Pierre-Nicolas Perrier and Rose-Adélaïde Jouët. A floral, Chardonnay-influenced style; the Belle Époque bottle carries Émile Gallé's 1902 anemone design.
w116.region: Champagne: France's northernmost major wine region. Chalk subsoils and a cool climate give racy acidity; the bubbles come from a second fermentation in bottle.

w010.palate: Dense yet supple; long, mineral finish.
w010.producer: Pomerol's most famous estate: about 11.5 ha on a unique buttonhole of iron-rich blue clay at the top of the plateau. Almost pure Merlot, run by the Moueix family.
w010.region: Pomerol, Bordeaux: a small Right Bank plateau of clay and gravel. Merlot dominates, giving plush, rich wines.
w010.vineyard: The blue-clay buttonhole on the highest part of the Pomerol plateau.

w011.palate: Massive and firm; built for decades.
w011.producer: Pauillac estate owned by the Rothschild family since 1853. Promoted to first growth in 1973, the only change ever made to the 1855 classification. Since 1945 each label has featured work by a different artist.
w011.region: Pauillac, Bordeaux: Left Bank home of three first growths. Deep gravel over limestone gives firm, Cabernet-led wines that age for decades.

w012.producer: Pauillac estate owned by the Rothschild family since 1853. Promoted to first growth in 1973, the only change ever made to the 1855 classification. Since 1945 each label has featured work by a different artist.
w012.region: Pauillac, Bordeaux: Left Bank home of three first growths. Deep gravel over limestone gives firm, Cabernet-led wines that age for decades.

w013.producer: The only first growth outside the Médoc, in Pessac on the edge of Bordeaux city. Documented as a wine estate since the 1500s and owned by the Dillon family since 1935.
w013.region: Pessac-Léognan, Bordeaux: the northern Graves, on gravel soils on the city's edge. Smoky, earthy, elegant reds.

w014.producer: The only first growth outside the Médoc, in Pessac on the edge of Bordeaux city. Documented as a wine estate since the 1500s and owned by the Dillon family since 1935.
w014.region: Pessac-Léognan, Bordeaux: the northern Graves, on gravel soils on the city's edge. Smoky, earthy, elegant reds.

w015.producer: Saint-Estèphe second growth, sitting just across the stream from Lafite in Pauillac. Founder Louis-Gaspard d'Estournel traded with India and built the oriental pagoda-topped cellars.
w015.region: Saint-Estèphe, Bordeaux: the Médoc's northernmost great commune. More clay than Pauillac, giving sturdier, slower-maturing wines.

w118.palate: Polished and dense, yet fresh and long.
w118.producer: Saint-Estèphe second growth, sitting just across the stream from Lafite in Pauillac. Founder Louis-Gaspard d'Estournel traded with India and built the oriental pagoda-topped cellars.
w118.region: Saint-Estèphe, Bordeaux: the Médoc's northernmost great commune. More clay than Pauillac, giving sturdier, slower-maturing wines.

w117.producer: Pessac-Léognan classed growth, owned by the Wilmers family since 1998, prized for finesse rather than power. It keeps a plot of very old, pre-phylloxera vines with mixed varieties.
w117.region: Pessac-Léognan, Bordeaux: the northern Graves, on gravel soils on the city's edge. Smoky, earthy, elegant reds.

w016.palate: Ethereal and silky, with Burgundian lift.
w016.producer: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's most singular estate, run by Emmanuel Reynaud. Pure Grenache from cool, sandy soils at very low yields, aged in old wood. Réservé is the grand vin.
w016.region: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, southern Rhône: warm, Grenache-led blends grown on soils ranging from large round stones to sand.
w016.vineyard: Rayas sits on sandy, north-facing plots surrounded by woodland, unusually cool for Châteauneuf.

w017.producer: Morgon estate. Marcel Lapierre (d. 2010) was a founding figure of natural wine, following Jules Chauvet's low-sulphur methods. Now run by his children Mathieu and Camille.
w017.region: Morgon, Beaujolais: one of the ten crus. Granite and schist soils give Gamay more depth and age-worthiness.

w063.nose: Rose, tar, sour cherry, dried herbs.
w063.producer: Barolo village estate famous for tradition: Bartolo, then his daughter Maria Teresa, kept to one blended Barolo from four crus, long fermentations and large old casks.
w063.region: Barolo, Piedmont: Nebbiolo grown in the Langhe hills. High tannin and acidity, rose and tar aromas, long-lived.
w063.vineyard: A blend of Cannubi, San Lorenzo and Rué in Barolo, plus Rocche dell'Annunziata in La Morra.

w064.producer: Monforte d'Alba family estate run by Claudio Fenocchio. Traditional long macerations and large casks, with holdings in several top crus including Bussia, Villero and Cannubi.
w064.region: Barolo, Piedmont: Nebbiolo grown in the Langhe hills. High tannin and acidity, rose and tar aromas, long-lived.
w064.vineyard: Villero: a south-facing cru in Castiglione Falletto, structured and perfumed.

w065.producer: Historic Barolo family house (no relation to Giuseppe Rinaldi), with holdings in the Brunate and Cannubi crus and a traditional, large-cask style.
w065.region: Barolo, Piedmont: Nebbiolo grown in the Langhe hills. High tannin and acidity, rose and tar aromas, long-lived.
w065.vineyard: Brunate: a great amphitheatre-shaped cru straddling La Morra and Barolo; powerful yet fragrant.

w066.producer: Barbaresco's most famous name, led by Angelo Gaja and now his children. Pioneered single-vineyard wines and modern techniques in Piedmont.
w066.region: Langhe, Piedmont: the hills around Alba. The Langhe DOC covers wines made outside the strict Barolo and Barbaresco rules.
w066.vineyard: From Cerequio, a top Barolo cru on the La Morra border. 'Conteisa' means 'contested', after an old dispute over the land.

w067.producer: Small family estate in Barolo village, run by Federico Scarzello, making traditional, elegant Barolo and Barbera.
w067.region: Alba, Piedmont: Barbera d'Alba is the region's juicy, high-acid everyday red; Superiore means longer ageing.

w069.producer: Collio estate in Friuli near the Slovenian border, known for long skin-contact whites from local varieties such as Ribolla Gialla.
w069.region: Collio, Friuli: hills on the Slovenian border with marl and sandstone (ponca) soils, famous for textured whites.

w070.producer: Puglian growers' co-operative founded in 1962 in San Marzano. Anniversario 62 is its old-vine Primitivo di Manduria.
w070.region: Manduria, Puglia: hot, sunny southern Italy, home of rich, ripe Primitivo (the same grape as Zinfandel).

w071.producer: Oakville joint venture between Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild, first vintage 1979. It makes essentially one wine, a Cabernet-led Bordeaux-style blend.
w071.region: Napa Valley, California: warm, sunny valley famed for ripe, polished Cabernet Sauvignon; Oakville is its heartland.
w071.vineyard: Estate vineyards in Oakville, including part of the historic To Kalon vineyard.

w072.producer: Leading family estate in Spitz in the Wachau, run by Franz Hirtzberger. Smaragd is the Wachau's top ripeness category for dry wines.
w072.region: Wachau, Austria: steep terraces above the Danube. Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; Smaragd is the ripest, fullest category.
w072.vineyard: Honivogl: a top site at Wösendorf on deep, sandy loess soils; richer, fuller wines.

w068.producer: Tenuta San Guido, home of Sassicaia: the Incisa della Rocchetta family planted Cabernet on the Tuscan coast in the 1940s, and the first commercial release was the 1968 vintage.
w068.region: Bolgheri, Tuscany: coastal hills where Bordeaux varieties thrive. Sassicaia was the first 'Super Tuscan' and now has its own DOC.

w019.producer: Samuel Billaud worked for years at his family's Billaud-Simon domaine before launching his own label. Precise, mineral Chablis from Petit Chablis up to grand cru.
w019.region: Chablis: Burgundy's northern outpost. Kimmeridgian limestone, rich in fossil oyster shells, gives taut, saline Chardonnay.
w019.vineyard: Petit Chablis comes from the plateaus around the slopes, on younger Portlandian limestone.

w020.producer: With Raveneau, one of Chablis' two benchmark traditional estates. Organically farmed, fermented and aged in old barrels, and famously long-lived.
w020.region: Chablis: Burgundy's northern outpost. Kimmeridgian limestone, rich in fossil oyster shells, gives taut, saline Chardonnay.
w020.vineyard: La Forest (often spelled Forêt) is part of the Montmains premier cru, on the left bank; firm and long-lived.

w021.nose: Lemon, white flowers, oyster shell, flint.
w021.palate: Fine and saline; tension with some depth.
w021.producer: With Raveneau, one of Chablis' two benchmark traditional estates. Organically farmed, fermented and aged in old barrels, and famously long-lived.
w021.region: Chablis: Burgundy's northern outpost. Kimmeridgian limestone, rich in fossil oyster shells, gives taut, saline Chardonnay.
w021.vineyard: La Forest (often spelled Forêt) is part of the Montmains premier cru, on the left bank; firm and long-lived.

w022.producer: Founded in Morey-Saint-Denis in 1968 by Jacques Seysses, now run by his sons Jeremy and Alec. Known for whole-cluster fermentation and perfumed, silky wines.
w022.region: Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte de Nuits: the largest red-wine village, with nine grands crus. Deep, firm, dark-fruited Pinot Noir.
w022.vineyard: Aux Combottes: a premier cru surrounded by grands crus (Latricières, Mazoyères and Clos de la Roche), and often treated as near-grand cru.

w023.nose: Red cherry, crushed stems, spice, earth.
w023.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w023.region: Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte de Nuits: the largest red-wine village, with nine grands crus. Deep, firm, dark-fruited Pinot Noir.
w023.vineyard: Clos des Varoilles: a walled premier cru monopole high in a side valley west of Gevrey village; cool and fresh.

w024.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w024.region: Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte de Nuits: the largest red-wine village, with nine grands crus. Deep, firm, dark-fruited Pinot Noir.
w024.vineyard: Chambertin-Clos de Bèze: grand cru planted by monks of Bèze Abbey in the 7th century, next to Le Chambertin. Prieuré Roch's 2023 crop was over the AOC yield limit, so rather than drop the extra, the domaine declared it all and sold it as Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru 'Réserve'.

w025.producer: Leading Gevrey-Chambertin estate. After Denis Mortet's death in 2006 his son Arnaud took over and has moved to a finer, more elegant style.
w025.region: Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte de Nuits: the largest red-wine village, with nine grands crus. Deep, firm, dark-fruited Pinot Noir.
w025.vineyard: A blend of five village-level Gevrey sites.

w026.producer: Gevrey-Chambertin family domaine founded by Alain Burguet, now run by his sons. Old vines and dark, concentrated wines; Symphonie is its old-vine village cuvée.
w026.region: Gevrey-Chambertin, Côte de Nuits: the largest red-wine village, with nine grands crus. Deep, firm, dark-fruited Pinot Noir.

w027.producer: Grand cru monopole in Morey-Saint-Denis, founded by Cistercian nuns in 1141. It has had only four owners in nearly 900 years, most recently the Pinault family's Artémis group (2017).
w027.region: Morey-Saint-Denis, Côte de Nuits: between Gevrey and Chambolle, combining structure and perfume. Four and a half grands crus.
w027.vineyard: 7.5 ha walled monopole between Bonnes-Mares and Clos des Lambrays. Its rows run north–south across the slope, unusual in Burgundy.

w028.producer: Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine, now run by Nicolas Raphet, with old vines in several grands crus including Clos de la Roche and Chambertin-Clos de Bèze.
w028.region: Morey-Saint-Denis, Côte de Nuits: between Gevrey and Chambolle, combining structure and perfume. Four and a half grands crus.
w028.vineyard: Clos de la Roche: Morey's largest and most powerful grand cru, on stony limestone.

w029.producer: Chambolle-Musigny domaine run by Ghislaine Barthod, who took over from her father Gaston. It holds many Chambolle premiers crus and bottles each separately to show its site.
w029.region: Chambolle-Musigny, Côte de Nuits: thin, limestone-rich soils give the Côte's most delicate, perfumed Pinot Noir.
w029.vineyard: Aux Beaux Bruns: a premier cru on the northern side of Chambolle, darker and firmer in style.

w030.producer: Chambolle-Musigny domaine run by Ghislaine Barthod, who took over from her father Gaston. It holds many Chambolle premiers crus and bottles each separately to show its site.
w030.region: Chambolle-Musigny, Côte de Nuits: thin, limestone-rich soils give the Côte's most delicate, perfumed Pinot Noir.
w030.vineyard: Les Chatelots: a premier cru just above the village; delicate and perfumed.

w031.producer: Beaune house founded in 1859, with large vineyard holdings across the Côte d'Or plus négociant purchases.
w031.region: Vougeot, Côte de Nuits: dominated by the walled grand cru Clos de Vougeot, built by Cistercian monks.
w031.vineyard: Clos de Vougeot: a 50 ha walled grand cru created by Cistercian monks, now split among about 80 owners.

w119.nose: Dark cherry, rose, forest floor, spice.
w119.palate: Ripe 2020 fruit with firm grand cru frame.
w119.producer: Laurent Ponsot ran his family's Domaine Ponsot in Morey for decades, and famously exposed counterfeit 'Ponsot' wines at auction. He left in 2017 to found his own house with his son Clément; each cuvée is named after a tree.
w119.region: Vougeot, Côte de Nuits: dominated by the walled grand cru Clos de Vougeot, built by Cistercian monks.
w119.vineyard: Clos de Vougeot: a 50 ha walled grand cru created by Cistercian monks, now split among about 80 owners.

w032.producer: Vosne-Romanée domaine (formerly Robert Arnoux) transformed by Charles Lachaux since the 2010s: more whole bunches, lighter extraction and a finer style.
w032.region: Vosne-Romanée, Côte de Nuits: Burgundy's most famous village, home of La Romanée-Conti and other legendary grands crus. Silky, spicy Pinot Noir.
w032.vineyard: Échezeaux: a large grand cru above Clos de Vougeot; quality varies by plot.

w033.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w033.region: Vosne-Romanée, Côte de Nuits: Burgundy's most famous village, home of La Romanée-Conti and other legendary grands crus. Silky, spicy Pinot Noir.
w033.vineyard: Les Suchots: a premier cru between Échezeaux and Romanée-Saint-Vivant, often rated near grand cru quality.

w034.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w034.region: Vosne-Romanée, Côte de Nuits: Burgundy's most famous village, home of La Romanée-Conti and other legendary grands crus. Silky, spicy Pinot Noir.
w034.vineyard: Les Hautes-Maizières: a village site just below Romanée-Saint-Vivant.

w035.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w035.region: Vosne-Romanée, Côte de Nuits: Burgundy's most famous village, home of La Romanée-Conti and other legendary grands crus. Silky, spicy Pinot Noir.

w036.producer: Vosne-Romanée domaine now run by Sébastien Cathiard. Small production of polished, highly sought-after wines.
w036.region: Nuits-Saint-Georges, Côte de Nuits: the southern end of the Côte de Nuits, with no grands crus but many fine, sturdy premiers crus.
w036.vineyard: Aux Murgers: a premier cru at the northern end of Nuits, near Vosne; finer and more fragrant than the south.

w037.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w037.region: Nuits-Saint-Georges, Côte de Nuits: the southern end of the Côte de Nuits, with no grands crus but many fine, sturdy premiers crus.
w037.vineyard: Clos des Corvées: a walled 5 ha premier cru monopole in Prémeaux, with old vines.

w038.producer: Founded in 1988 by Henri-Frédéric Roch, co-director of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and nephew of Lalou Bize-Leroy. Since his death in 2020 it has been run by Yannick Champ. Organic, whole bunches, minimal sulphur; based in Prémeaux.
w038.region: Nuits-Saint-Georges, Côte de Nuits: the southern end of the Côte de Nuits, with no grands crus but many fine, sturdy premiers crus.
w038.vineyard: Clos des Corvées: a walled 5 ha premier cru monopole in Prémeaux.

w039.producer: Vosne-Romanée domaine now run by Sébastien Cathiard. Small production of polished, highly sought-after wines.
w039.region: Hautes-Côtes de Nuits: the cooler hills behind the Côte de Nuits. Lighter, fresher wines, increasingly good in warm years.

w040.producer: Vosne-Romanée domaine now run by Sébastien Cathiard. Small production of polished, highly sought-after wines.
w040.region: Hautes-Côtes de Nuits: the cooler hills behind the Côte de Nuits. Lighter, fresher wines, increasingly good in warm years.

w041.producer: Small family estate working organically in the Côte de Beaune.
w041.region: Savigny-lès-Beaune, Côte de Beaune: a side valley north of Beaune making supple, fragrant reds.
w041.vineyard: Les Lavières: a premier cru on the Beaune side of Savigny, named for its flat stones (laves).

w042.producer: Small family estate working organically in the Côte de Beaune.
w042.region: Beaune: the wine capital of Burgundy, with a large hillside of premiers crus giving round, generous reds.
w042.vineyard: Les Grèves: one of Beaune's finest premiers crus, on gravelly (grève) soils mid-slope.

w043.producer: Volnay family domaine making fresh, finely structured reds from Volnay and Pommard.
w043.region: Pommard, Côte de Beaune: clay-rich soils make it the Côte de Beaune's firmest, most structured red.
w043.vineyard: Les Rugiens: Pommard's top premier cru, on red, iron-rich soils; powerful and long-lived.

w045.producer: Small family estate working organically in the Côte de Beaune.
w045.region: Volnay, Côte de Beaune: thin limestone soils give the Côte de Beaune's most elegant, perfumed reds.
w045.vineyard: Les Caillerets: Volnay's top premier cru, on stony limestone.

w046.producer: Volnay family domaine making fresh, finely structured reds from Volnay and Pommard.
w046.region: Volnay, Côte de Beaune: thin limestone soils give the Côte de Beaune's most elegant, perfumed reds.

w047.producer: Volnay family domaine making fresh, finely structured reds from Volnay and Pommard.
w047.region: Volnay, Côte de Beaune: thin limestone soils give the Côte de Beaune's most elegant, perfumed reds.

w048.producer: Volnay family domaine making fresh, finely structured reds from Volnay and Pommard.
w048.region: Volnay, Côte de Beaune: thin limestone soils give the Côte de Beaune's most elegant, perfumed reds.

w044.producer: Volnay's reference domaine, biodynamic since 2000 and run by Frédéric Lafarge. Classic, long-lived wines.
w044.region: Volnay, Côte de Beaune: thin limestone soils give the Côte de Beaune's most elegant, perfumed reds.
w044.vineyard: Les Caillerets: Volnay's top premier cru, on stony limestone.

w050.producer: Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine with holdings in Bâtard-, Criots-Bâtard- and Le Montrachet.
w050.region: Puligny-Montrachet, Côte de Beaune: a high water table means no cellars, and its whites are the most finely chiselled in Burgundy.
w050.vineyard: Bâtard-Montrachet: the grand cru just below Le Montrachet, straddling Puligny and Chassagne. Deeper soils give richer wines.

w051.producer: Brothers Marc and Alexandre Bachelet, who began in 2005 and quickly built a name for taut, precise Puligny and Chassagne.
w051.region: Puligny-Montrachet, Côte de Beaune: a high water table means no cellars, and its whites are the most finely chiselled in Burgundy.
w051.vineyard: Les Folatières: Puligny's largest premier cru, on the slope above the village.

w052.producer: Meursault domaine of François Mikulski, known for lively, mineral whites.
w052.region: Meursault, Côte de Beaune: the largest white-wine village, known for richer, nutty Chardonnay. No grands crus.
w052.vineyard: Les Meix Chavaux: a village site on the slope above Meursault; fresh and bright.

w053.producer: One of several Boillot family domaines in the Côte de Beaune.
w053.region: Meursault, Côte de Beaune: the largest white-wine village, known for richer, nutty Chardonnay. No grands crus.
w053.vineyard: Les Clous: a village site high on the slope above Meursault, cool, stony and mineral.

w054.producer: Small family estate working organically in the Côte de Beaune.
w054.region: Meursault, Côte de Beaune: the largest white-wine village, known for richer, nutty Chardonnay. No grands crus.
w054.vineyard: Les Clous: a village site high on the slope above Meursault, cool, stony and mineral.

w049.producer: Puligny-Montrachet's benchmark white Burgundy estate. Anne-Claude Leflaive led its move to biodynamics in the 1990s.
w049.region: Puligny-Montrachet, Côte de Beaune: a high water table means no cellars, and its whites are the most finely chiselled in Burgundy.
w049.vineyard: Chevalier-Montrachet: the grand cru directly above Le Montrachet. Thinner, stonier soils give tighter, more mineral wines.

w057.producer: Alex Moreau made the wines at Bernard Moreau et Fils for years; from 2021 he has bottled his share of the family vineyards under his own name.
w057.region: Chassagne-Montrachet, Côte de Beaune: shares the Montrachet grands crus with Puligny. Whites are a little broader; some reds too.
w057.vineyard: Morgeot: Chassagne's largest premier cru, in the south of the village; broader and richer whites.

w058.producer: Alex Moreau made the wines at Bernard Moreau et Fils for years; from 2021 he has bottled his share of the family vineyards under his own name.
w058.region: Chassagne-Montrachet, Côte de Beaune: shares the Montrachet grands crus with Puligny. Whites are a little broader; some reds too.
w058.vineyard: Morgeot: Chassagne's largest premier cru, in the south of the village; broader and richer whites.

w059.producer: Alex Moreau made the wines at Bernard Moreau et Fils for years; from 2021 he has bottled his share of the family vineyards under his own name.
